terms.gloss: an empire: rule over other peoples, and the lands it covers
evidence: Cic. Rep. 6.16: ut mē imperiī nostrī paenitēret (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First the power to command; then dominion, and the realm itself, “especially frequent since the Augustan period” (Lewis & Short). The Roman Empire is imperium populī Rōmānī (Liv. 3.26.8); Morgan–Owens uses imperium for modern empires too.

evidence: Caes. BG 2.34: in diciōnem potestātemque populī Rōmānī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Found only in the oblique cases (Lewis & Short): in diciōnem redigere, to bring under one’s rule. Morgan–Owens uses it for the lands of an empire.

phrases.latin: spēs ūnica imperiī populī Rōmānī L. Quīnctius trāns Tiberim … quattuor jūgerum colēbat agrum
phrases.english: the one hope of the Roman people’s empire, Lucius Quinctius, was farming a field of four iugera across the Tiber
Bulgaria was part of the Ottoman Empire.
